title: The City of Labtayt
logline: A tower stays sealed under twenty-four locks, one from every king, until a new king from another house ignores his advisers, opens it, and finds stone riders and a written warning that comes true the same year.
moral: A warning kept by generations deserves a hearing; some doors cannot be closed again once opened.
tone: A legend told with a straight face: ritual and mystery in the first half, a cold reveal in the middle, wonder in the treasure hall, and a quiet, rueful ending. Humour is small and comes from the bystanders (the guard, the nobles, a curious child), never from the conquest.

beats.summary: A sealed tower in the citadel of Labtayt.
Every king adds a lock: the counter reaches 24.
Nobody knows what the tower hides; kings look away from it.
A new king from another family arrives.
He decides to open the door.
The elders try to stop him; he refuses advice.
He refuses their gold as well.
All the locks come off: counter back to 0.
Stone Arab riders on horses and camels with swords and spears.
The written warning: an army like these riders, and the fall of the land.
Fear, and the door is already open.
The living army arrives in the statues' formation, led by Tariq ibn Ziyad; the crown falls.
The treasure hall and its wonders: crowns, books, instruments, the mirror, the table.
The treasures go to the Caliph al-Walid.
The tower is remembered for a warning heard too late.

sets.description: NEW, reusable walled city on a hill. World 1600 x 1230, ground y 900. Library sky + hillTrees behind. Plain x 900..1600. City wall: band y 640..900 from x 0 to 900, paper stone with brown block lines, crenellations 40 wide every 80; gate arch at x 500 (140 wide, 190 tall, two leaves that open); small gate towers either side to y 560. Behind the wall 9 flat-roofed houses in three rising rows (tops y 600, 520, 450), yellow, paper and red-dot walls, small blue windows, two domes. Citadel on top: wall y 380..450 from x 380 to 800; the tower at x 570..710 from y 250 to 450, NAVY with blue dots (the only dark building), crenellated, with a small arched door at its foot and a window slit at y 300. Option {locks, open} draws the small door state; option flag.

NEW close view of the tower front. World 1000 x 1230, ground y 900. Navy stone wall with blue Ben-Day dots and block lines fills x 120..880 up to y 120 (crenellations above, sky behind); paved ground. Door: arch x 350..650, sill y 900, spring line y 520, arch top y 380; two brown plank leaves with black iron bands, a 6 px gap between; a stone step 30 high in front. Fields: locks 0..24 (padlocks on a 6 x 4 grid, slot centres x 390 + 44*col, y 530 + 80*row; each padlock 34 wide x 44 tall: yellow body, black shackle arc, keyhole dot; lock 1 is 1.4x and sits on a chain across the middle), open 0..1 (leaves rotate inward as two parallelograms narrowing to 20 % width, showing a black interior), ivy 0..1, time u for skyCycle, heap n (fallen locks pile at x 700..820). Exposes lockSlot(i) and fallen-lock positions.

NEW interior of the tower, reusable as any vault or crypt. World 1000 x 1230, floor y 900. Dark navy wall with large stone blocks, three shallow arched niches on the back wall (tops y 300), floor of paper flagstones in perspective bands. Doorway: bright arch at the left, x 40..260, top y 400. Field open 0..1 gives the light: a paper-yellow wedge on the floor from the doorway toward x 960 and a pale vertical band on the back wall; everything outside the wedge is drawn at 35 % brightness (multiply navy). Low plinth: top y 860, x 330..960. Scroll niche in the left wall at (160, 560), 90 x 120. Seeded dust motes inside the wedge.

PLANNED palaceHall (AN-045, AN-095, KD-017, KD-031), used in two dressings. Treasury: three arches on the back wall, shelf at y 520 (x 180..660), worktable at x 680..920 top y 760, a double door at the left that opens toward the viewer. Throne bay (S13): one arch, a bench throne with cushions at x 620, carpet.
PLANNED desertRoad travel strip (AN-044, AN-095): scrolling dunes, a foreground palm trunk used for the wipe at 154.66.

props.description: padlock(ctx, x, y, {s, shut, rust}) and the lock grid of towerDoor: yellow body 34 x 30 with rounded corners, black shackle arc 14 radius (open = shackle rotated 40 degrees), keyhole. Reusable for any locked chest or door.
PLANNED scroll (AN-095): paper sheet 90 x 120 between two brown rollers, open 0..1, squiggle lines only (never readable text).
Treasure chest 170 x 110 (brown planks, yellow bands, domed lid with open 0..1) holding the planned coinPile; part of treasureHoard.
PLANNED crownProp (AN-046) with shape variants: 0 round three-point (old house), 1 tall pointed with red jewel (new king), 2..6 for the shelf (band with pearls, spiked, domed, small circlet, dented).

NEW treasureHoard module, one small function per item so later palace stories reuse them: coin mound (planned coinPile at 260 wide), gem chest (open box with 9 diamond shapes in red, blue, green), vessels (ewer 60 x 130, bowl 110 x 50, cup 40 x 60, yellow with red dot shading), books (stack of 5 slabs 110 x 24 in red, blue, brown plus one open book with a page flip field), instruments (alembic: flask circle r 34 with a 90 long downward beak on a tripod; astrolabe: brass disc r 40 with a rotating pointer and ring; the planned balanceScale; tongs).

Great mirror: oval glass 260 x 380 in a gold frame 18 thick with 8 red studs, on a two-foot stand; content(ctx) callback drawn clipped inside the glass; cover cloth as a keyed red polygon. Part of treasureHoard.

The precious table: top 320 x 26 gold with a green inlay band and a row of 9 small pearls, four turned legs 150 tall with red and blue stones, on a carpet 380 x 20. Always shown empty and with no figure near its centre. Part of treasureHoard.
PLANNED sword (AN-082) drawn curved, 150 long, plus a spear: shaft 300 long x 6 brown, leaf tip 40 x 18, small red pennant option. Both take a stone flag for the statues.

subtitles.ar: تحكي رواية قديمة عن مدينة في الأندلس اسمها لبطائط،|كانت فيها قلعة ذات برج مغلق.|كلما مات ملك وجاء ملك جديد،|وضع قفلًا آخر على باب البرج، حتى صار عليه أربعة وعشرون قفلًا.
subtitles.en: An old tale speaks of Labtayt,|a city in al-Andalus with a sealed tower.|Each new king added a lock|until its door held twenty-four.

subtitles.ar: لم يكن أحد يعرف ما يخفيه البرج.|وكان الملوك السابقون يتركونه مغلقًا، فلا يدخلونه ولا يسمحون لغيرهم بفتحه.|ثم جاء ملك جديد من أسرة غير الأسرة التي حكمت من قبله.
subtitles.en: No one knew what lay inside.|Earlier rulers had kept it sealed,|until a new king from another family took power.

subtitles.ar: نظر الملك الجديد إلى الأقفال الكثيرة، وقرر فتح الباب.|حاول كبار رجال الدولة منعه،|وقالوا إن الملوك السابقين تركوه مغلقًا لسبب مهم.|لكنه لم يقبل نصيحتهم وأصر على الدخول.
subtitles.en: The new king decided to open the tower.|His advisers warned that previous kings|must have had a reason to keep it shut,|but he insisted.

subtitles.ar: عرض عليه الرجال أموالهم وكنوزهم إذا غير رأيه.|لم ينفع العرض، فأمر بنزع الأقفال كلها.|وعندما فتح الباب، وجد تماثيل لفرسان عرب|على خيول وجمال، يحملون السيوف والرماح.
subtitles.en: His nobles even offered him wealth to change his mind.|He refused, removed the locks,|and found figures of Arab riders|bearing swords and spears.

subtitles.ar: رأى الملك صحيفة مكتوبة، فقرأ فيها تحذيرًا|يقول إن فتح البرج سيجلب جيشًا يشبه أولئك الفرسان،|وسيكون سببًا في سقوط البلاد.|ارتعب الحاضرون، لكن الباب كان قد فتح بالفعل.
subtitles.en: A written warning said|opening the tower would bring an army like the riders shown|and lead to the country’s fall.|The witnesses were frightened, but the door was already open.

subtitles.ar: تقول الحكاية إن جيشًا عربيًا بقيادة طارق بن زياد|وصل إلى الأندلس في السنة نفسها.|هزم الملك ودخل المدينة،|ووجد فيها كنوزًا عظيمة من الذهب والحجارة الكريمة والأواني النفيسة.
subtitles.en: The legend says that in that same year|an Arab army led by Tariq ibn Ziyad reached al-Andalus,|defeated the king|and discovered immense treasure.

subtitles.ar: كانت هناك تيجان كثيرة، وكتب قديمة،|وأدوات عجيبة تتحدث الرواية عن قدرتها على تحويل المعادن.|ووجدوا أيضًا مرآة كبيرة قيل إنها تُظهر صور البلاد البعيدة،|وطاولة ثمينة نُسبت إلى سليمان عليه السلام.
subtitles.en: Among the treasures were crowns, old books,|marvelous instruments,|a mirror said to show distant lands,|and a precious table attributed to Solomon.

subtitles.ar: أرسلت الكنوز، كما تروي القصة، إلى الخليفة الوليد بن عبد الملك.|أما البرج الذي ظل مغلقًا أجيالًا طويلة،|فقد ارتبط في ذاكرة الناس بتحذير|لم يسمعه الملك الجديد إلا بعد فوات الأوان.
subtitles.en: The treasures were sent, the tale says, to Caliph al-Walid.|The tower, sealed for generations,|became remembered for a warning|the new king heeded too late.

new_assets.name: horse
new_assets.description: Side-view comic horse for this and any rider, caravan or farm story. About 380 wide x 300 tall at s 1 (back at 190, ears at 300), feet at (x, y), facing dir. Palettes: 0 bay (brown, black mane), 1 white (paper with blue dots), 2 black. Fields: ph, amp (walk and gallop), rear 0..1, headDown, talk (neigh), mane and tail follow-through, saddle (cloth colour), plus the shared acting fields. Exposes saddlePoint and bob for a rider.
new_assets.implementation: Build like the Library deer and lion: rounded-box body 240 x 110, neck quad rising 110 at 55 degrees, wedge head 110 x 60 with one eye (eye2), nostril, two pointed ears; four two-segment legs driven by walk(posFn, t) (gallop = pairs offset by 0.5 phase with amp 1.3); mane as 5 overlapping brush triangles along the neck, tail as a tapering brush stroke using swing(). Halftone shading with the existing dot fill. Wrap with acting() and add a registry entry.

new_assets.name: mountedRider
new_assets.description: A person seated on a mount (horse, planned camel, later donkey): rideOn(mountFn, mountP, personP, {weapon}). The rider is drawn from the hips up (front-facing torso and head as the Library person, clipped at the saddle line), one flat leg shape hanging on the near side with a stirrup, hips at the mount saddlePoint, following its bob with a 2-frame lag and lurching on a stop. weapon: sword or spear in the raised hand via aR angles.
new_assets.implementation: Draw order: far-side nothing, mount, then ctx.save + clip rect above the saddle line + person(ctx, {...P, x: sx, y: sy + 130*s}) + restore, then a near-side leg (rounded rect 26 x 80 in the robe colour plus shoe) and the saddle cloth edge over the cut. Uses the existing lurch idea from the Monkey film (guide section 6, passenger riding a carrier). Matches the planned camel rider field; implement once and use for both.

new_assets.name: statueTint
new_assets.description: Draw any Library character or group as carved stone: one grey-paper tone with blue-grey dot shading, black outlines kept, no blinking; amount 0..1 cross-fades between stone and full colour (used for the statue-to-army match).
new_assets.implementation: Bake the group once to an offscreen canvas with bake(); copy it through ctx.filter = 'grayscale(1) contrast(0.85) brightness(1.05)', then multiply a flat #cfc7b4 rectangle with globalCompositeOperation 'multiply' clipped by 'destination-in' to the group alpha, and overlay the Halftone Pop dot pattern at 20 %. For amount between 0 and 1 draw the colour bake under it and the stone bake at alpha = amount. Pure function of the pose, so deterministic. Related to the planned stoneFigure (AN-082) and ghostForm: share the bake-and-tint helper.

new_assets.name: hillCity
new_assets.description: Walled hill city with gate, stepped houses, citadel and one dark tower (dimensions under sets). Reusable for any city, siege, arrival or "once in a city" opening; options: gate open, flag, tower door state, time of day.
new_assets.implementation: Rectangles and arcs only: wall band with a crenellation loop, houses from a seeded table of [x, top, w, colour], domes as half circles, block lines with K.rng seeded strokes. Bake once per state with bake(); sky via skyCycle behind.

new_assets.name: towerDoor
new_assets.description: Close view of a great locked door in a stone tower with fields locks 0..24, open 0..1, ivy, heap, time of day (dimensions under sets). Reusable as any palace, treasury or prison door.
new_assets.implementation: Bake the wall; draw leaves and locks live. Leaves: two quads whose inner edges move toward the jambs with open (width factor 1 to 0.2) with black behind. padlock() is a rounded rect plus an arc; the grid is a loop over lockSlot(i). Falling locks are scene sprites using fallY and rebound from each slot to a heap slot.

new_assets.name: towerChamber
new_assets.description: Dark vault interior lit by a wedge of light from a doorway, with a plinth and a wall niche (dimensions under sets). Reusable for crypts, cellars, treasure vaults and caves with a door.
new_assets.implementation: Bake the lit version of the room; each frame draw it, then draw a navy rectangle at alpha 0.65 with the light wedge polygon cut out (evenodd clip, as in the Fox film head-into-hole clip). Characters and statues are drawn before the darkness layer so they are revealed by the wedge edge. Dust motes: 30 seeded dots drifting with K.noise, drawn only inside the wedge.

new_assets.name: treasureHoard
new_assets.description: Module of palace treasure items: chest, gem chest, vessels, books, instruments (alembic, astrolabe, tongs), the great mirror with a content callback, and the jewelled table (dimensions under props). Uses the planned coinPile, crownProp, balanceScale and goldGlow.
new_assets.implementation: One function per item from rectangles, ellipses and diamonds in the palette (yellow with red dot shading for gold, flat red, blue and green for stones). Mirror: ctx.save, ellipse clip, content(ctx), restore, then frame and a diagonal glint band.

new_assets.name: padlock
new_assets.description: Single padlock with shut 0..1 and rust option; also drawn by towerDoor.
new_assets.implementation: Rounded rect body, shackle arc rotated about its right foot when open, keyhole circle plus wedge.

owner_questions: Tariq ibn Ziyad is shown as a calm, dignified mounted figure with a name label (default: shown, face visible, never comic); confirm, or ask for him to be seen only from behind or at a distance.

The table attributed to Solomon (peace be upon him) is shown as an empty jewelled table in a cone of light with the label "THE TABLE OF SOLOMON" and no figure of the prophet anywhere (default); confirm the label wording.
The defeat of the king is softened: no battle or wounded people, only a dust cloud, the crown falling from the wall and the king ducking out of sight (default); confirm.
The death of each earlier king is shown only as the crown lifting off and the figure fading (default); confirm.

The king and his court are dressed with the Library caliph, vizier and merchant presets recoloured (the story does not name them); a more European Visigothic look would need a new costume preset (default: recoloured existing presets).
Invented bystanders not in the script: a door guard, a curious child and two townspeople, plus the end image of the former king sitting on the tower step (default: included).

Invented English lettering: SEALED, 24 LOCKS!, NO ENTRY!, OPEN IT!, WAIT!, NO!, TOO LATE!, THE SAME YEAR!, TREASURE!, ACHOO!, GOLD?, and the legend tags (THE LEGEND SAYS..., SO THE TALE SAYS, IT IS SAID) that keep the story framed as a tale (default: included).
The alchemy instruments show a grey lump becoming a gold coin with the label "GOLD?" and the tag "SO THE TALE SAYS" (default: shown as a claim of the tale, with the question mark).
implementation_notes: Copy Library/template to Animations/AN-085; build timing.json from planning/inputs/timeline.json and use the word times given here (all cue.t values are word starts on the final MP3).
Subtitles: write chunks_ar.txt and chunks_en.txt from the subtitles array (| marks) and verify against story/script.json by program.

Direction of travel carries meaning: old kings and the new king enter from the LEFT; the statues face LEFT; the army rides right to left in the same poses; the treasure leaves left to RIGHT. Keep it consistent.
Define the five rider poses once (RIDERS = [{mount, x, y, s, weapon, aR, pal}...]) and use the same table for the statues (S7, S8), the thought cloud (S8) and the army (S10) so the match is exact.

Lock counter: one function lockCount(t) from kfn keys (1 at 9.9; 2 at 15.56; 5 at 17.6; 20 at 19.9; 21, 22, 23 at 20.2, 20.8, 21.3; 24 at 21.82; down from 24 at 72.66 to 0 at 74.06) drives the door, the counter and the click sounds.

The narration has almost no pauses (only 6.6-6.9, 10.52-10.92, 22.36-22.64 and after 171.08). Every other effect is placed on a word boundary: keep them under 120 ms, at gain 0.25 or less, and drop any that masks a consonant when you listen.
Set LIFE.t = t each frame for automatic blinks, but give the stone riders noBlink and no gaze changes; their stillness is the effect.
Use panel-only shake for the lock snaps and the crown bounce; the caption panel never moves.
Earlier kings as memories: draw with the planned dream wash at alpha 0.55 above the door (y 150..360) so they never cover faces or the lock grid.
